TopicPrompt: Reckless decisions like that put everyone at risk.
ResponseText: But that kind of reflection is fruitless... I made the final call. The burden lies on my shoulders.

TopicPrompt: Reckless decisions like that put everyone at risk.
ResponseText: I hope, at least, you can start to see things from my perspective more... To understand why I make the choices I make.

TopicPrompt: Shin told me a bit. Sounds like he was guilty, too.
ResponseText: No. I was the commanding officer. Blame starts at the top. That's one subject the two of us agree on, even if he doesn't realize it.
When we lost Alan, Shin stepped up to take on many of his responsibilities. On top of the grief... that must have been a lot to handle.
It led him to fall back on what he knows: rules and doctrine. He doesn't trust anyone else to help him see beyond that. Not like he trusted Alan.
And because of me... because of a call I made, we all lost him. I know Shin will never forgive me for it.

TopicPrompt: I wonder if things would have been different if he were here.
ResponseText: Almost certainly.

TopicPrompt: Seems like he was a great man.
ResponseText: Indeed. He was the bedrock of this team... And things were never the same with Shin from then on.
Sometimes I think... no, I'm certain, that I was selected for this mission in order to remove my perspective and influence.
The Elders saw my pull and experience as a threat, and knew I would never align with their goals...
What better way to prevent my meddling than to send me packing on a cross country venture?
I often wonder... if they ever expected me to report in at all. To make it here alive... Joke's on them, I guess.

TopicPrompt: Sounds like you didn't know what you were signing up for.
ResponseText: No, I don't think it's quite as simple as a bait and switch.

TopicPrompt: Sounds like you didn't know what you were signing up for.
ResponseText: When the founders started out, I genuinely believe they were fueled by a desire to protect people from the horrors of the old world.

TopicPrompt: Sounds like you didn't know what you were signing up for.
ResponseText: But time changed them... Paid too much attention to what they did and how, but lost sight of why: the people.

TopicPrompt: Sounds like it was a good fit.
ResponseText: It was. Even knowing what I know now, I have no regrets. They were my people, my comrades.

TopicPrompt: Sounds like it was a good fit.
ResponseText: But things changed as time rolled on... As I'm sure you know, the views of the Elders and I... differed greatly.

TopicPrompt: Let's finish with a toast.
ResponseText: I think that's a fine idea. To whom?

ResponseText: Oh cut the crap, I'm being real here. There's some things we need to hash out. C'mon, pull up a stool.

TopicPrompt: No. Let's go.
ResponseText: I just... Fine. Let's get on with it, then.

ResponseText: All the more reason we shouldn't blow our cover. Blending in a bit first might help with that.

TopicPrompt: People's lives are at risk. We don't have time for this.
ResponseText: Well? I'm buying, pal. Whaddya say?

TopicPrompt: We are not friends, Rahmani.
ResponseText: Clearly. But we aren't adversaries either.

ResponseText: I understand. You're anxious to continue this investigation, but we've been through a lot. It'd be good to iron some things out.

TopicPrompt: Sure, I could use a drink.

ResponseText: But, listen... I was hoping we could talk for a few minutes before we head upstairs.
Let me buy you a drink. What do you say?

TopicPrompt: What's with the get-up? I barely recognized you.
ResponseText: (sigh) You're a little slower on the draw than I thought. It's to keep a low profile... To not draw attention... Am I getting through?

If there's somethin' I can tell ya that'll help find my Cassie, just ask.

Finally decided that ol' Knapp was worth helpin' out? Well, ask if ya got questions... If it'll help find Cassie, that is.

TopicPrompt: That's all for now.
ResponseText: Just get her home safe, please. She means the world to me.

ResponseText: Oh, well, she's tough as nails and twice as sharp. The girl is like a... whaddayacallit... prodigy for farm work.

TopicPrompt: What can you tell me about your niece Cassie?
ResponseText: She wrote sayin' she's moving to Foundation. Share her knowledge and such. Sounded like a load of hooey to me, but I'd love to see her all the same.

ResponseText: 'Cause Cassie said so herself! Or, at least, her letters did. She called 'em out by name a few times. Said she hired them to provide safe travel.

TopicPrompt: Why are you so sure Blue Ridge is involved?
ResponseText: 'Course, when I went an' asked 'em myself they played the fool. "No, sir, we deliver cargo, not people." Bunch'a lying sons a... Every one of 'em.

ResponseText: Look out, here comes trouble.

TopicPrompt: Agreed. I've got your back.

TopicPrompt: Don't you think you're jumping to a few too many conclusions?

We've always been up-front and honest with this venture. The routes are dangerous, and our Brahmin sure as hell don't smell like roses.
Everyone who works with us gets the straight truth, and I certainly don't take too kindly to what you're implyin'.
I could stand here and deny your allegations every which way to Sunday, but I know you won't just take my word for it.

Slow down, Paladin, this is not an admission of guilt, or an attempt to weasel out of responsibility.
We are just as concerned about these folk as you. We are willing to cooperate in hopes of saving lives, nothing else.
If you're hoping I'm about to spill the beans on some secret abduction scheme, you're out of luck. We have the same goals as you in this.
I'd be offended by these accusations, if it didn't weave such a fascinating story. Are you planning to sell that as a dime novel?
Well... If you're wondering why my organization would choose to dodge your calls, examine the attitude with which you've started this conversation.
This pseudo-authority you're flaunting is exactly the type of oppression and regulation that my free enterprise can do without.
Honeyed words... But we should proceed. What can you tell us about the people that went missing from your caravan?
Better to just let you take a look for yourselves.
Aries! C'mon in here.
You rang, boss?
Harpers Ferry. The train tunnel. Mind showing our guests the route?
Oh crap. You really want to go back there?
That was exactly my thinkin', Aries. Head on over to that tunnel and show this duo of detectives the scene of the crime.
Does that sound amenable to y'all?

ResponseText: You've lost that many people!? And we're only just now hearing about this?

Absolutely not.

I will... take your word for it. I am sorry, either way.

An unfortunate end, but there's still hope of finding them. The only thing left is to report back our findings and determine Blackburn's location.
The caravan was ambushed by armed strangers, likely the Hellcat Mercenaries you fought.
Based on the manifest, a "Dr. Blackburn" attended every trip where someone went missing. Including the final one.
All of the evidence together points to one clear answer...

So I guess we'll need to find a way to change "Open Sesame Seed" into a series of numbers.
Now we just need a way to change that phrase into a series of numbers.

From the sound of it, they wrote the numbering system down so they wouldn't need to remember it... Must be around here somewhere.

Looks like we'll need more than just a password to get through... Some kind of code for turning words into numbers, it seems.

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]
TopicPrompt: Protocol Adonais -- what does that even mean?

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]
TopicPrompt: Protocol Adonais -- what does that even mean?

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]
TopicPrompt: Protocol Adonais -- what does that even mean?
ResponseText: So, I made a plan: if the moment came, I'd record one myself. It... ended up going on a little longer than expected.

QuestName: [Dialogue quest for Named NPCs near Big Bend]
TopicPrompt: Protocol Adonais -- what does that even mean?
ResponseText: In the end, I guess it's just a journal of my thoughts... and instead of proving my death, it's proof I'm still alive.

ResponseText: Uh huh.
Really? Vinny told me you were asking if I could be put on this shift with you.
He even said you were willing to do back to back runs to make it happen...
Hello, Kieran. Good seeing you again.
Oh, hi Libby! I didn't know you were on duty for this run.
Fine... Safe.
Carver. This is the wrong time, I'm the wrong person, and that was definitely the wrong way to do it.
So, how's the family?
I... Okay, that's embarrassing. I was just hoping to...
No.
Very true. There are things far more deadly than a gang of would-be bandits in those hills. Trust me on that one.
You... get used to it.
Maybe we sent them running. You know, got 'em good and scared.
How are you so calm, Libby?
Oh, that's right. You're pretty new to Blue Ridge. But, no, not so much. Big Bend is its own special nightmare for us merchants.
Not much choice in the matter, though. Believe it or not, it's the safest route to the western side of this mountain range.
They know we're a threat now. I'm sure word has gotten back to the rest of their crew.
Do any other routes see this much action?
Definitely not. So keep a tight formation, watch all sides. Keep cover on the Brahmin.
Alright, well, let's get a move on.
I guess that means this isn't going to get any easier, will it?
Right, well, let's get moving.
Libby, I... uh... I'm good. Thanks for asking.
Well, this'll be a fun trip.
(Cough)
Look, let's take it from the top: Hi Carver, how are you today?
That's good... Good. And my community is also fine and safe, thank you for asking.
I'm, uh, don't know what you mean, I was just...
Ooh that was a mean one, nice going!
Just remember that I can't protect these Brahmin by myself!
Cold, Aries. I like it.
But don't leave me and the Brahmin to fend for ourselves! We're pretty exposed down here.
Alright, take it slow. No telling what's ahead.
Okay, let's see what these sneaky little eaglets have waiting for us...
Easy now... Don't let them get the drop on us.
Not again...
Okay, here we go. We got this.
Don't forget about the Brahmin! They'll be gunning for them.
Blood Eagles, incoming!
Ah, shit. Blood Eagles, incoming!
Contact, we've got contact!
I'm alive! And I've still got wares to sell! Thank you! Let's head outside.
Looks like we're in the clear. Good work.
Make a break for it! Go, go, go!
There's an opening. Let's move out while we can.
We've got a clearing, now's our chance. Move, double time!
Enemies incoming. We need to hold up here. Watch our flanks, they'll come from all sides.
Here they come! Watch the rear, we're surrounded. We have to hold out until we can get an opening.
Don't let those Brahmin out of your sight!
Damn! Another ambush! Hold out here as long as we can! Eyes on our 6, we're prone to an attack from the rear.
You hear that?
I like you, Aries, but you're freaking me the hell out.
Hold. Something isn't right.
I expected more retaliation for taking down a captain.
Do you feel that? A steady tremble from the dark. They approach.
Hrmm... Stop messing around.
(sigh) Just when I starting to like you, Carver...
Of course I did, but look how I've finally got you talking, Kieran. Tell me, how was your childhood?
Yeah, I wasn't sure we'd make it out of there. Thanks for having my back.
But, um... do you think you could make that an Old Possum instead?
Golly. I can't wait.
The cliffs above makes travel by Brahmin too slow, too dangerous. The lack of cover leaves us vulnerable.
There are no roads that won't lead to a fight. At least this way is favorable for fighting larger numbers.
I would have thought you knew that, Eugenie.
We're not out of the woods yet. We just killed one of their captains. They're going to get a little... vengeful.
Well fought. Good job, crew. Remind me to buy everyone a round of Blackwater Brew after this is over.
That was a tough fight. Why don't we try taking the roads over the mountains next time?
Phew... We're alive. We are alive, right?
Alright... We're doing okay. Making good time. Still breathing.
Don't leave us waiting too long, we're easy pickings here!
Well done, the captain is down. The control for the gate is up top.
Damn. They've got the gate closed. Looks heavily guarded.
That one up top looks like a captain. We need to take him out first.
Bastards. They closed the gate. The button is above us, but looks like they're holed in there pretty good.
Tough guy up top looks like their boss. Let's pay him our respects and get that gate open.
More coming! They're going full force because they knew the "ghoul merchant" was coming through.
They always think we're a quick score... Let's make them regret it.
We've got more incoming. Look alive!
Whoa! There's more of 'em coming!
Blockade ahead. We'll need to knock it down. I'll set some charges to clear the rubble. Watch my back.
They must be looking to stall us. Expect a serious fight ahead.
Hm. Blockade ahead. What are they playing at. Leave the clean-up to me. You just watch for ambushes.
Hold up. We've got a blockade ahead. They must be trying to buy time.
I'll take care of the wall, everyone else watch our six. They'll probably be on us any second.
That was practically an army. We must have gotten them all, right?
I didn't think they'd come at us this hard... This isn't even a large shipment.
Man, they aren't messing around today.
No. This is just the start. Don't let your guard down.
It's always kill or be killed with Blood Eagles. Can't even give them an inch.
That's never made a difference to them before. Don't can't let your guard down.
Okay, stay sharp. Everyone hold position.
Wait, quiet. We've got trouble.
And you're standing around making jokes? Everyone, ready-up for a fight!
Well, looking to be smooth sailing today, we--
Whoa, Libby, I'm just messing around. Listen we've got some Blood Eagle reports coming in, so, uh...
It sounded like they've already overrun the second checkpoint. They'll be on us any minute.
Oh you know, just another waltz through this magical tunnel.
Can't this ever be easy?
Kieran, Eugenie. How ya'll doing?
Well, well, if it isn't the two youngin's out for a stroll. Did Vinny say it was okay for you guys to be out without a chaperone?
Oh good, you're here. We've got trouble, Blood Eagles, lots of them.
Hrm.
Okay, I get what you mean. Let's keep moving.
Not that there's ever any shortage of hooligans to kill and treasure to find.
Oh, right. Thanks, Libby! I appreciate, the uh...
Uh huh...
Don't know what you're talking about, Rudy, keep up.
Right: our priority is protecting the Brahmin, not going on a killing spree or a treasure hunt.
That's right. They'll try to attack from the rear when they see an opening so watch our backs.
Glad your head's in the game, Carver.
Oh, and if anyone wants to scout ahead, there may be some extra cargo lying around from our less successful ventures.
Just don't forget about the Brahmin.
Oh, and uh, it'd be good if you could stick close to the Brahmin. You never know when an attack will come.
What was that part about "even at the cost of Rudy's life?" Did I hear that right?
Protect the Brahmin at all costs. Even at the sake of your own, or Rudy's, life. If we lose the Brahmin, we lose our pay.
If you get lucky, you may spot some cargo that was lost on previous runs. We'll pay for that too. Let's head out.
Hrmm... Let's move out.
You'll be paid for what makes it to the other side. Protecting the Brahmin is our top priority.
And if you spot any loose cargo lying around, we'll provide a bonus, but do not leave those Brahmin vulnerable.
We'll be carrying a load of premium arms and ammunition, so I'd appreciate an extra touch of care.
Hopefully the reward for getting me there in one piece will more than compensate for any bullets you... invest.
We're just hauling some furniture and furs, but so far that hasn't stopped the Blood Eagles from trying to rob us.
Hi Rudy.
It did not.
I don't think I could picture you doing something more mundane. Kieran the fisherman. Kieran the bar tender. Kieran the... professional singer.
So... I'm guessing it didn't work out, huh?
Yes. Many times in the past.
Ever consider a less dangerous line of work, Kieran?
No, but the caps don't hurt.
See the world and all that? Maybe I'm a Marine after all. Dad must be so proud.
You know, I've been doing this traveling merchant thing for a while now.
I spent damn near a decade stuck in our compound, hiding from people that would kill us on sight just for being who we are.
I've found that rolling into town with supplies and caps to trade eases up the tension, get's people talkin' to you again.
The fact that I'm strapped to the teeth in fire power doesn't hurt neither. But some people, like the Blood Eagles... there's no discussion to be had.
If you don't mind me asking, why did you become a caravan guard, Libby?
So what were you up to before this caravan gig?
So you're saying we're unqualified for this job? Would you like to step down here so I can provide a sample of my qualifications?
(Chuckle)
That's a box you don't want to open.
The fuck, Aries?
Let's hope no one is going to any graves today... Other than our enemies, as we cast their forsaken souls to hell itself.
Their screams echoing back as our merciless assault rips them from this mortal coil. Darkly we stride, tall and powerful, through this tunnel of death.
The usual, food, water, various delicious secret family recipes that I'll take to the grave. That sort of thing.
Rudy. What are we hauling today?
Agreed. Let's move out! Make for the exit!
Now seems as good a time as any!
Well done, we're in the clear. Let's head out there while we can.
Solid work, crew... Mission accomplished. Now, let's head outside before more of them show up.
We... made it... Hoo! We made it!
I think... we lost 'em. Thanks, guys. Happy to still be breathing.
Not a chance... Tread carefully.
Is it just me, or has it gotten really quiet? Think we've seen the last of them?
I can understand that... Plus, we get to travel.
Caps, right? Bet it was the caps.
Exactly. If we hesitate, we die.
For years, I could barely breathe through the blood caked up in my throat. But little by little I found my footing again.
Even back then, there all sorts of shit you could get mixed up in. Mistakes you made weren't just wiped clean when the bombs fell.
So, I searched, and searched, until I didn't. That life ended with this caravan route. Found something here that gave me a reason to stay.
Honestly? Just needed a reason to get away from my family for a while.
I guess I can count myself lucky to have any family left at all... But, I never really found my place with them.
My dad was a Marine, and in a lot of ways he still is. Like living with a drill sergeant. Mom is no better, she had a military background, too.
My brother and sister are great at helping around the camp, but... it's not for me. I've always been a good shot, so I may as well get paid for it.
We've still got some, uh, enemy resistance down here. Let's get that gate open soon please?
These stragglers don't look to "demoralized," though, so help keep these Brahmin safe!
Their captain is dead. Good going. Get the gate open and let's clean up the stragglers.
Target down. Well done. The button to open the gate should be up there as well.
We're going to have to cut through. Looks like there's a captain up top. He's our priority target.
